terms.gloss: a speaking helper: a voice assistant
evidence: Plin. NH 10.141: avēs cantū aliquō aut hūmānō sermōne vōcālēs (Lewis & Short s.v. vōcālis)
terms.comment: A description of ours: adjūtor, a helper, with vōcālis, that speaks, Pliny’s word for birds that talk. No reference work has a word for a voice assistant. One that answers in writing is an adjūtor artificiālis (see chatbot).

phrases.latin: Clārius loquere; adjūtor vōcālis tē nōn audit.
phrases.english: Speak more clearly; the voice assistant can’t hear you.

phrases.latin: Rogā tēlephōnum quae hodiē tempestās futūra sit.
phrases.english: Ask the phone what the weather will be today.

sources: Lewis & Short: vocalis · Lewis & Short: adjutor
